           │ > For a railroad crossing a control system needs to be developed that on receipt of a signal indicating that a train is approaching closes the gates, │
           │ and only opens these gates after the train has sent a signal indicating that it crossed the road. The requirement that should be met by the control   │
           │ system is that the gates are always closed when the train is crossing the road. The complete system consists of the three components Train, Gate, and │
           │ Controller: Train || Gate || Controller.  Model this system. You can assume that all trains pass the relevant track section in the same direction.    │
           │ Detail: The states of the transition system for the Train have the following intuitive meaning: in state "far" the train is not close to the          │
           │ crossing, in state "near" it is approaching the crossing and has just sent a signal to notify this, and in state "in" it is at the crossing. The      │
           │ states "up" and "down" of the Gate have the obvious interpretation. The controller has 4 states 0, 1, 2 and 3. It changes from state 0 to 1 when the  │
           │ train is approaching, from state 1 to 2 when the gate is lowering, from state 2 to 3 when the train is exiting the crossing, and from state 3 to 0    │
           │ when the gate is raising. The state changes of the Controller stand for handshaking with the trains (via the actions approach and exit) and the Gate  │
           │ (via the actions lower and raise via which the Controller causes the gate to close or to open, respectively). Use the variable names train_state,     │
           │ controller_state and gate_state.  Make sure that you satisfy the following specifications: Based on the natural language description provided, we can │
           │ generate the following invariants for the system: 1. When the train is at the crossing (train_state = in), the gate must be down (gate_state = down): │
           │ train_state = in => gate_state = down 2. The controller state must change according to the following rules:   a. From state 0 to state 1 when the     │
           │ train is approaching (train_state = near):     controller_state = 0 => controller_state' = 1 if train_state = near   b. From state 1 to state 2 when  │
           │ the gate is lowering (gate_state = down):     controller_state = 1 => controller_state' = 2 if gate_state = down   c. From state 2 to state 3 when    │
           │ the train is exiting the crossing (train_state = far):     controller_state = 2 => controller_state' = 3 if train_state = far   d. From state 3 to    │
           │ state 0 when the gate is raising (gate_state = up):     controller_state = 3 => controller_state' = 0 if gate_state = up 3. The controller state      │
           │ should always be in the range [0, 3]:   0 <= controller_state <= 3 These invariants ensure that the gates are always closed when the train is         │
           │ crossing the road, and that the controller behaves according to the specified rules.                                                                  │

           │ > For a railroad crossing a control system needs to be developed that on receipt of a signal indicating that a train is approaching closes the gates, │
           │ and only opens these gates after the train has sent a signal indicating that it crossed the road. The requirement that should be met by the control   │
           │ system is that the gates are always closed when the train is crossing the road. The complete system consists of the three components Train, Gate, and │
           │ Controller: Train || Gate || Controller.  Model this system. You can assume that all trains pass the relevant track section in the same direction.    │
           │ Detail: The states of the transition system for the Train have the following intuitive meaning: in state "far" the train is not close to the          │
           │ crossing, in state "near" it is approaching the crossing and has just sent a signal to notify this, and in state "in" it is at the crossing. The      │
           │ states "up" and "down" of the Gate have the obvious interpretation. The controller has 4 states 0, 1, 2 and 3. It changes from state 0 to 1 when the  │
           │ train is approaching, from state 1 to 2 when the gate is lowering, from state 2 to 3 when the train is exiting the crossing, and from state 3 to 0    │
           │ when the gate is raising. The state changes of the Controller stand for handshaking with the trains (via the actions approach and exit) and the Gate  │
           │ (via the actions lower and raise via which the Controller causes the gate to close or to open, respectively). Use the variable names train_state,     │
           │ controller_state and gate_state.  Make sure that you satisfy the following specifications: Based on the natural language description provided, we can │
           │ generate the following invariants for the system: 1. When the train is at the crossing (train_state = in), the gate must be down (gate_state = down): │
           │ train_state = in => gate_state = down 2. The controller state must change according to the following rules:   a. From state 0 to state 1 when the     │
           │ train is approaching (train_state = near):     controller_state = 0 => controller_state' = 1 if train_state = near   b. From state 1 to state 2 when  │
           │ the gate is lowering (gate_state = down):     controller_state = 1 => controller_state' = 2 if gate_state = down   c. From state 2 to state 3 when    │
           │ the train is exiting the crossing (train_state = far):     controller_state = 2 => controller_state' = 3 if train_state = far   d. From state 3 to    │
           │ state 0 when the gate is raising (gate_state = up):     controller_state = 3 => controller_state' = 0 if gate_state = up 3. The controller state      │
           │ should always be in the range [0, 3]:   0 <= controller_state <= 3 These invariants ensure that the gates are always closed when the train is         │
           │ crossing the road, and that the controller behaves according to the specified rules.                                                                  │

           │ > For a railroad crossing a control system needs to be developed that on receipt of a signal indicating that a train is approaching closes the gates, │
           │ and only opens these gates after the train has sent a signal indicating that it crossed the road. The requirement that should be met by the control   │
           │ system is that the gates are always closed when the train is crossing the road. The complete system consists of the three components Train, Gate, and │
           │ Controller: Train || Gate || Controller.  Model this system. You can assume that all trains pass the relevant track section in the same direction.    │
           │ Detail: The states of the transition system for the Train have the following intuitive meaning: in state "far" the train is not close to the          │
           │ crossing, in state "near" it is approaching the crossing and has just sent a signal to notify this, and in state "in" it is at the crossing. The      │
           │ states "up" and "down" of the Gate have the obvious interpretation. The controller has 4 states 0, 1, 2 and 3. It changes from state 0 to 1 when the  │
           │ train is approaching, from state 1 to 2 when the gate is lowering, from state 2 to 3 when the train is exiting the crossing, and from state 3 to 0    │
           │ when the gate is raising. The state changes of the Controller stand for handshaking with the trains (via the actions approach and exit) and the Gate  │
           │ (via the actions lower and raise via which the Controller causes the gate to close or to open, respectively). Use the variable names train_state,     │
           │ controller_state and gate_state.  Make sure that you satisfy the following specifications: Based on the natural language description provided, we can │
           │ generate the following invariants for the system: 1. When the train is at the crossing (train_state = in), the gate must be down (gate_state = down): │
           │ train_state = in => gate_state = down 2. The controller state must change according to the following rules:   a. From state 0 to state 1 when the     │
           │ train is approaching (train_state = near):     controller_state = 0 => controller_state' = 1 if train_state = near   b. From state 1 to state 2 when  │
           │ the gate is lowering (gate_state = down):     controller_state = 1 => controller_state' = 2 if gate_state = down   c. From state 2 to state 3 when    │
           │ the train is exiting the crossing (train_state = far):     controller_state = 2 => controller_state' = 3 if train_state = far   d. From state 3 to    │
           │ state 0 when the gate is raising (gate_state = up):     controller_state = 3 => controller_state' = 0 if gate_state = up 3. The controller state      │
           │ should always be in the range [0, 3]:   0 <= controller_state <= 3 These invariants ensure that the gates are always closed when the train is         │
           │ crossing the road, and that the controller behaves according to the specified rules.                                                                  │

           │ > For a railroad crossing a control system needs to be developed that on receipt of a signal indicating that a train is approaching closes the gates, │
           │ and only opens these gates after the train has sent a signal indicating that it crossed the road. The requirement that should be met by the control   │
           │ system is that the gates are always closed when the train is crossing the road. The complete system consists of the three components Train, Gate, and │
           │ Controller: Train || Gate || Controller.  Model this system. You can assume that all trains pass the relevant track section in the same direction.    │
           │ Detail: The states of the transition system for the Train have the following intuitive meaning: in state "far" the train is not close to the          │
           │ crossing, in state "near" it is approaching the crossing and has just sent a signal to notify this, and in state "in" it is at the crossing. The      │
           │ states "up" and "down" of the Gate have the obvious interpretation. The controller has 4 states 0, 1, 2 and 3. It changes from state 0 to 1 when the  │
           │ train is approaching, from state 1 to 2 when the gate is lowering, from state 2 to 3 when the train is exiting the crossing, and from state 3 to 0    │
           │ when the gate is raising. The state changes of the Controller stand for handshaking with the trains (via the actions approach and exit) and the Gate  │
           │ (via the actions lower and raise via which the Controller causes the gate to close or to open, respectively). Use the variable names train_state,     │
           │ controller_state and gate_state.  Make sure that you satisfy the following specifications: Based on the natural language description provided, we can │
           │ generate the following invariants for the system: 1. When the train is at the crossing (train_state = in), the gate must be down (gate_state = down): │
           │ train_state = in => gate_state = down 2. The controller state must change according to the following rules:   a. From state 0 to state 1 when the     │
           │ train is approaching (train_state = near):     controller_state = 0 => controller_state' = 1 if train_state = near   b. From state 1 to state 2 when  │
           │ the gate is lowering (gate_state = down):     controller_state = 1 => controller_state' = 2 if gate_state = down   c. From state 2 to state 3 when    │
           │ the train is exiting the crossing (train_state = far):     controller_state = 2 => controller_state' = 3 if train_state = far   d. From state 3 to    │
           │ state 0 when the gate is raising (gate_state = up):     controller_state = 3 => controller_state' = 0 if gate_state = up 3. The controller state      │
           │ should always be in the range [0, 3]:   0 <= controller_state <= 3 These invariants ensure that the gates are always closed when the train is         │
           │ crossing the road, and that the controller behaves according to the specified rules.                                                                  │

           │ > For a railroad crossing a control system needs to be developed that on receipt of a signal indicating that a train is approaching closes the gates, │
           │ and only opens these gates after the train has sent a signal indicating that it crossed the road. The requirement that should be met by the control   │
           │ system is that the gates are always closed when the train is crossing the road. The complete system consists of the three components Train, Gate, and │
           │ Controller: Train || Gate || Controller.  Model this system. You can assume that all trains pass the relevant track section in the same direction.    │
           │ Detail: The states of the transition system for the Train have the following intuitive meaning: in state "far" the train is not close to the          │
           │ crossing, in state "near" it is approaching the crossing and has just sent a signal to notify this, and in state "in" it is at the crossing. The      │
           │ states "up" and "down" of the Gate have the obvious interpretation. The controller has 4 states 0, 1, 2 and 3. It changes from state 0 to 1 when the  │
           │ train is approaching, from state 1 to 2 when the gate is lowering, from state 2 to 3 when the train is exiting the crossing, and from state 3 to 0    │
           │ when the gate is raising. The state changes of the Controller stand for handshaking with the trains (via the actions approach and exit) and the Gate  │
           │ (via the actions lower and raise via which the Controller causes the gate to close or to open, respectively). Use the variable names train_state,     │
           │ controller_state and gate_state.  Make sure that you satisfy the following specifications: Based on the natural language description provided for the │
           │ railroad crossing control system, the following invariants can be derived: 1. Whenever the train is at the crossing (train_state = "in"), the gate    │
           │ must be down (gate_state = "down"). Mathematically: train_state = "in" -> gate_state = "down". 2. When the train is approaching the crossing          │
           │ (train_state = "near"), the controller must be in state 1 (controller_state = 1). Mathematically: train_state = "near" -> controller_state = 1. 3.    │
           │ Once the gate is lowered (gate_state = "down"), the controller must be in state 2 (controller_state = 2). Mathematically: gate_state = "down" ->      │
           │ controller_state = 2. 4. When the train is exiting the crossing (train_state = "far"), the controller must be in state 3 (controller_state = 3).      │
           │ Mathematically: train_state = "far" -> controller_state = 3. 5. After the gate is raised (gate_state = "up"), the controller must return to state 0   │
           │ (controller_state = 0). Mathematically: gate_state = "up" -> controller_state = 0. These invariants ensure that the desired behaviors and             │
           │ requirements of the system are met at all times, guaranteeing the safety and proper functioning of the railroad crossing control system.              │

           │ > For a railroad crossing a control system needs to be developed that on receipt of a signal indicating that a train is approaching closes the gates, │
           │ and only opens these gates after the train has sent a signal indicating that it crossed the road. The requirement that should be met by the control   │
           │ system is that the gates are always closed when the train is crossing the road. The complete system consists of the three components Train, Gate, and │

           │ Detail: The states of the transition system for the Train have the following intuitive meaning: in state "far" the train is not close to the          │

           │ states "up" and "down" of the Gate have the obvious interpretation. The controller has 4 states 0, 1, 2 and 3. It changes from state 0 to 1 when the  │
           │ train is approaching, from state 1 to 2 when the gate is lowering, from state 2 to 3 when the train is exiting the crossing, and from state 3 to 0    │
           │ when the gate is raising. The state changes of the Controller stand for handshaking with the trains (via the actions approach and exit) and the Gate  │
           │ (via the actions lower and raise via which the Controller causes the gate to close or to open, respectively). Use the variable names train_state,     │

           │ property makes explicit the critical requirement that the gate must be closed when the train is at the crossing, aligning with the main safety goal   │

           │ raising (transition back to state 0) once the train has completely exited and the gate is confirmed to be closed. [Hint 5] Provide a specification    │

           │ > For a railroad crossing a control system needs to be developed that on receipt of a signal indicating that a train is approaching closes the gates, │
           │ and only opens these gates after the train has sent a signal indicating that it crossed the road. The requirement that should be met by the control   │
           │ system is that the gates are always closed when the train is crossing the road. The complete system consists of the three components Train, Gate, and │
           │ Controller: Train || Gate || Controller.  Model this system. You can assume that all trains pass the relevant track section in the same direction.    │
           │ Detail: The states of the transition system for the Train have the following intuitive meaning: in state "far" the train is not close to the          │
           │ crossing, in state "near" it is approaching the crossing and has just sent a signal to notify this, and in state "in" it is at the crossing. The      │
           │ states "up" and "down" of the Gate have the obvious interpretation. The controller has 4 states 0, 1, 2 and 3. It changes from state 0 to 1 when the  │
           │ train is approaching, from state 1 to 2 when the gate is lowering, from state 2 to 3 when the train is exiting the crossing, and from state 3 to 0    │
           │ when the gate is raising. The state changes of the Controller stand for handshaking with the trains (via the actions approach and exit) and the Gate  │
           │ (via the actions lower and raise via which the Controller causes the gate to close or to open, respectively). Use the variable names train_state,     │
           │ controller_state and gate_state. [Hint 1] Introduce a specification to check if transitions between states in `controller_state` correctly process    │
           │ and react to `train_state` changes. This will involve validating that controller transitions from state 0 to 1 when a train signal for approaching    │
           │ (state "near") is received, and likewise, controller must transition from state 2 to 3 when a train has exited (state "in" to "far"). [Hint 2] Extend │
           │ the initial system description with a requirement for a safety property: "The `gate_state` must be 'down' whenever `train_state` is 'in'." This       │
           │ property makes explicit the critical requirement that the gate must be closed when the train is at the crossing, aligning with the main safety goal   │

           │ appropriate train and gate signals. This means the controller should only initiate lowering (transition to state 1) upon train approaching and        │
           │ raising (transition back to state 0) once the train has completely exited and the gate is confirmed to be closed. [Hint 5] Provide a specification    │

           │                                                                                                                                                       │
           │ > For a railroad crossing a control system needs to be developed that on receipt of a signal indicating that a train is approaching closes the gates, │
           │ and only opens these gates after the train has sent a signal indicating that it crossed the road. The requirement that should be met by the control   │
           │ system is that the gates are always closed when the train is crossing the road. The complete system consists of the three components Train, Gate, and │
           │ Controller: Train || Gate || Controller.  Model this system. You can assume that all trains pass the relevant track section in the same direction.    │
           │ Detail: The states of the transition system for the Train have the following intuitive meaning: in state "far" the train is not close to the          │
           │ crossing, in state "near" it is approaching the crossing and has just sent a signal to notify this, and in state "in" it is at the crossing. The      │
           │ states "up" and "down" of the Gate have the obvious interpretation. The controller has 4 states 0, 1, 2 and 3. It changes from state 0 to 1 when the  │
           │ train is approaching, from state 1 to 2 when the gate is lowering, from state 2 to 3 when the train is exiting the crossing, and from state 3 to 0    │
           │ when the gate is raising. The state changes of the Controller stand for handshaking with the trains (via the actions approach and exit) and the Gate  │
           │ (via the actions lower and raise via which the Controller causes the gate to close or to open, respectively). Use the variable names train_state,     │
           │ controller_state and gate_state. [Hint 1] The controller state transitions should be clearly specified for each action (approach, exit, lower, raise) │
           │ and should only occur under specific conditions. Consider detailing in the task description that the controller state should only transition from `0` │
           │ to `1` when `train_approaching` is true and `train_state` should transit from `far` to `near` appropriately to mimic the approach of the train. [Hint │
